# Verdict · Reissue a lost debit card

**Rework.** The journey blocks the card but leaves the user with no way to pay for 5–7 days, and a failed block ends in a generic error while the card stays active. All three P0 goals fit inside the current journey. If the bank cannot issue an instant virtual card (owner decision 1), the verdict becomes **Redesign**: half of the JTBD would then have no answer in the app.

Input: 37 findings (cjm 17 · edge 13 · load 7), all three families valid. Evidence: the AI map only. No screens, code or analytics; 73 % of steps are assumptions.

## Summary by family

| Family | Findings | Main point |
|---|---|---|
| CJM logic | 3 critical · 6 high · 7 medium · 1 low | "Keep paying today" has no stage; V1 and V3 are violated by content; the success ending sits at emotion −1 |
| Edge cases | 2 critical · 4 high · 6 medium · 1 low | All 3 synthetic personas finished `partial`; failed block has no way out; no path for a relative |
| Cognitive load | 3 high · 4 medium | No step above 50; flat load with no recovery step. Address typing is 25.3 of 45.2 s KLM. Exit points at s7, s8, s10 only for the low/low profile |

## Goals

| Goal | Pri | What must become true | Metric · target | Findings | Owner | Effort | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G-01 | P0 | After blocking, the user can pay today | Permanent blocks followed by a virtual card in the phone wallet within 10 min · ≥ 60 % | CJM-01, CJM-03, EDGE-02, LOAD-07 | business/content | L | 36.0 |
| G-02 | P0 | A failed block says the card is NOT blocked and offers retry and a 24/7 line | Failed blocks resolved (retry or call) within 10 min · ≥ 95 % | CJM-07, EDGE-01, CJM-08, LOAD-03 | engineering | M | 18.0 |
| G-03 | P0 | Blocking starts with one tap from the home screen | Taps from home to "card blocked" · 4 → 2 | CJM-02, LOAD-04 | design | M | 45.0 |
| G-04 | P1 | Fee and delivery date are known before the order form | Orders where fee and date were shown before s6 · 100 % | CJM-04, CJM-05, LOAD-02, EDGE-13 | product | M | 18.0 |
| G-05 | P1 | A relative knows on one screen what they may do for the cardholder | Relatives in test who name the allowed action · ≥ 4 of 5 | EDGE-05 | legal or domain review | S | 16.8 |
| G-06 | P1 | Choosing a block type cannot strand the user without a new card | Temporary blocks from "Lost or stolen" upgraded within 24 h · < 5 % | CJM-06, EDGE-03 (LOAD-05 as constraint) | design | M | 15.0 |
| G-07 | P1 | The blocked card and the order stay visible in the app until the new card is active | Users with a pending order who see its status on home · 100 % | CJM-10, CJM-15, EDGE-04 | product | M | 15.0 |
| G-08 | P1 | An unchanged address is confirmed without typing and shown on the summary | Orders with address confirmed without typing · ≥ 80 % | LOAD-01, CJM-13, EDGE-06 | design | M | 12.6 |

Score = severity × confidence × reach × impact × confirmation / effort (`skills/journey-verdict/references/prioritization.md`). G-03 is P0 by rule (violated vision item on the main job), not by order of score.

**P2** (no specs):

| Findings | Score | Fix hint |
|---|---|---|
| CJM-09, LOAD-06 | 7.5 | Replace BLOCKED_PERM and "reissue" with plain words (covered by G-02 copy for s5) |
| CJM-11, CJM-17 | 6.0 | Map revision: split s2; list invented facts in frame.md |
| CJM-16, EDGE-10 | 5.3 | Adjacent journey: transactions since the loss with "I did not make this" |
| EDGE-11 | 4.2 | Adjacent journey: block without the app; hotline on the public site |
| EDGE-07 | 4.2 | Keep the form draft; idempotent block request; state after reconnect |
| CJM-14 | 4.2 | Card design and name on card: prefilled from the old card, optional (owner decision 6) |

**Deferred:** EDGE-08 (double order on repeat tap, hypothesis), EDGE-09 (cancel order before shipping; the irreversibility line moved to G-06), EDGE-12 (several cards, low confidence).

## Conflicts

| What clashed | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| CJM-02 "remove or default the block-type question" vs LOAD-05 "keep it, useful friction" | Keep the dialog, preselect permanent when entered from "Lost or stolen" (G-03, G-06) | Permanent block is irreversible; the confirmation is a financial safeguard. Made faster, not removed |
| CJM-02 critical vs LOAD-04 medium on the same steps | Critical | Lead finding violates owner vision V1 |
| LOAD-02 "fee on the s5 button" vs CJM-05 "before the form" vs CJM-04 "date on s6 and s8" | Show fee and date on the s5 confirmation, repeat on s8 | One change satisfies all three; s8 only confirms known values |
| EDGE-03 (2 of 3 personas chose wrong) vs CJM-06 (provided failure note) | CJM-06 leads; EDGE-03 stays a hypothesis | Synthetic evidence adds weight, not class |
| LOAD-03 confidence low (30 s wait is from normalization) inside a critical cluster | Cluster keeps CJM-07 values; 30 s not used as a baseline | Lead finding sets confidence; the wait must be measured (G-02) |
| Script K-20 grouped EDGE-11 with LOAD-04 | Split: LOAD-04 → G-03, EDGE-11 → P2 | Different fixes: home entry vs blocking without the app |

## Keep

- **s5 relief "money is safe"**, the only point above zero. TO BE keeps the confirmation first and early; offers come below it.
- **s3 block-type confirmation** (useful friction, LOAD-05): faster with outcome labels and a default, still a deliberate tap.
- **s8 order summary**: stays as the final check of fee, date and address.

## TO BE

Default options of the owner decisions. Fork marked ⑂.

| Stage | User does | Sees | Response | Undo |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Notice | Opens the app | Home with balance; card tile with "Lost or stolen?" | — | — |
| 2. Block | Taps "Lost or stolen?" | Dialog: two options described by outcome, "Block for good and get a new card" preselected | — | Cancel |
| 3. Block | Taps "Block card" | "Blocking card •• 1234…" with expected time | Provider blocks the card | — |
| 3a. Block failed | — | "Your card is NOT blocked yet" · Try again · Call 24/7 block line | — | Try again |
| 4. Block | Reads the confirmation | "Card •• 1234 is blocked. Nobody can pay with it." · Pay today · Order a new card: fee, arrives by date | — | — |
| 5. Pay today ⑂ | Taps "Get a virtual card" | Virtual card ready · "Add to phone wallet" | Issues the virtual card | Skip |
| 6. Reissue | Taps "Order a new card" | Form: address from profile, design and name from the old card | — | Back |
| 7. Reissue | Confirms or edits the address | Prefilled address; typing only for a new one | — | Edit |
| 8. Reissue | Confirms the order | Summary: fee, delivery by date, address with Edit | Order accepted; status in the app | — |
| 9. Done | Returns to home | Card tile: "New card ordered, arrives by date" · virtual card active | Push on each status change | Track order |

- **Added:** 3a → G-02 · 5 → G-01 · status tile on 9 → G-07 · "Acting for someone else?" link on 2 → G-05
- **Changed:** 1–2 entry from the home tile → G-03 · 2 dialog labels and default → G-06 · 4 plain-language confirmation with fee and date → G-04, P2 · 6–7 prefilled address → G-08 · 8 address on summary → G-08 · 9 home tile → G-07
- **Removed:** old s2 "card settings with 9 actions" from the main path → G-03 (still reachable from the card screen)
- **Kept as useful friction:** 2 block-type confirmation (irreversible) · 8 summary before ordering

## Validation with people

Run first: tasks 1–3 (P0 goals, all on assumptions).

1. **G-01** · hypothesis: after blocking, users do not know how to pay today. Task: "You have just blocked your lost card. Buy a coffee with your phone." 5 commuters, 2 of them 55+. Success: ≥ 4 of 5 add the virtual card to the wallet within 3 min without help.
2. **G-03** · hypothesis: users look for blocking inside card settings. Task: "Your wallet is gone. Make sure nobody can use your card." 5 first-time users. Success: ≥ 4 of 5 reach the block dialog with one tap from home.
3. **G-02** · hypothesis: after a generic error users think the card is blocked. Task: prototype with forced failure; "Is your card safe now?" 5 users. Success: 5 of 5 answer "no" and pick retry or call.
4. **G-06** · hypothesis: low-literacy users pick temporary (EDGE-03). Task: "You will not find this wallet again. Block the card." 5 users 60+, large font. Success: ≥ 4 of 5 choose permanent and can say why.
5. **G-04** · hypothesis: the fee and the week without a card surprise users at s8. Task: order a new card, then "What will it cost and when will it arrive?" asked before the summary. 5 users. Success: ≥ 4 of 5 answer both correctly.
6. **G-08** · hypothesis: users moved in the last year do not check the address. Task: order a new card to a new home. 5 users who moved. Success: 5 of 5 notice and change the address before confirming.
7. **G-05** · hypothesis: relatives do not know whether they may act. Task: "Your father lost his card. Help him." 5 relatives of people 70+. Success: ≥ 4 of 5 name the allowed action within 1 min.

## Owner decisions

1. **Instant virtual card (V2).** Can the bank issue one right after a permanent block? Default: yes. If no: Redesign; options are a temporary card at a branch, cash by code at an ATM, or an honest "you cannot pay by card until <date>".
2. **Reissue fee for a lost card.** Charge, waive, or waive for theft. G-04 needs the rule and the amount.
3. **Delivery date.** A concrete date needs a logistics commitment. Options: "by <date>" from courier SLA; date range with calendar dates; "5–7 days" with the earliest date.
4. **Meaning of V1 "one tap".** Default: one tap opens the block dialog, the confirmation tap stays (irreversible action). Alternative: one tap blocks temporarily, permanent follows.
5. **Representatives.** May a relative block a card, order a reissue, change the address? Default: block only via the 24/7 line; reissue only by the cardholder. Needs legal review.
6. **Temporary → permanent.** Can a temporary block be upgraded in the app and still allow a reissue? Default: yes.
7. **Reissue form fields.** Keep card design and name on card, prefilled from the old card, or drop them.

## Not checked

- Map vs live product (L16): no screens, code or analytics. Specs describe the map; verify against the product before building.
- Real blocking and issuer wait times; text of the generic error; copy of the s3 dialog.
- Screen reader and keyboard (E10), entry from push or the bank's site (E01).
- Real emotions and moments of truth: all emotions set during normalization.
- Adjacent journeys not audited: disputes after theft, blocking without the app, tracking and activating the new card.

## Method notes

- Merged by meaning beyond the script: K-01 + K-03 (+ LOAD-07) → G-01; K-06 + K-07 → G-02; K-09 + K-14 → G-07; K-12 + K-18 → G-08; K-05 + K-16 (+ K-22 as constraint) → G-06; LOAD-04 moved from K-20 to G-03.
- CJM-12 (moments of truth unvalidated, script P1) is not a fix; it became validation tasks 4–5. CJM-17 moved to P2 map revision.
- EDGE-05 kept at P1 by rule "high on the main path", although most of its spec waits for owner decision 5.
- Confidence was not raised anywhere: EDGE-03, EDGE-06 and EDGE-13 remain synthetic; LOAD findings remain model outputs.
- Effort set by the verdict: S 1 · M 2 · L 3. G-01 is L because issuing and provisioning a virtual card may need a backend and a wallet integration.

# G-01 · P0 · After blocking, the user can pay today

## Problem
The JTBD is "nobody can spend my money **and** I keep paying today". The map ends on a home screen with no card at all, 5–7 days before the new one arrives (s10, emotion −1). Owner vision V2 (virtual card) has no step. All three synthetic personas finished `partial` here.
Findings: CJM-01 (critical, provided), CJM-03 (high, absent), EDGE-02 (critical, provided), LOAD-07 (medium, absent). Label: **business / content** — the goal changes the offer, not only a screen.

## Goal and metric
- Share of permanent blocks followed by a virtual card added to a phone wallet within 10 min · now: 0 % (no step) · target: ≥ 60 % (revise after 4 weeks of baseline) · how: `virtual_card_added_to_wallet` / `card_blocked{type=permanent}`.
- Share of block confirmations that show the pay-today option · target: 100 % · how: `pay_today_offer_shown`.

## Scope
- s5 confirmation → adds "Pay today" with a virtual card offer.
- New step: virtual card issued and added to the phone wallet.
- s10 → home tile shows the active virtual card.
- Out of scope: the physical card order (G-04, G-08), disputes of past charges (P2).

## TO BE journey (fragment)
| Step | User does | Sees | Response | Undo / way back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | Reads the block confirmation | "Card •• 1234 is blocked" · block "Pay today" · "Order a new card" | — | — |
| 5a | Taps "Get a virtual card" | "Your virtual card is ready" · card number hidden · "Add to phone wallet" | Issues the virtual card on the same account | Skip, continue to order |
| 5b | Taps "Add to phone wallet" | Wallet's own confirmation, then "Ready to pay" | Provisions the card to the wallet | Remove from wallet later |
| 9 | Returns to home | Tile "Virtual card · ready to pay" next to the order status | — | — |

## States
| State | What the user sees | What they can do |
|---|---|---|
| Default | Offer under the confirmation | Get the card, skip |
| Loading | "Creating your virtual card…" with expected time | Wait, leave (card arrives in app) |
| Error | "We could not create the virtual card. Your old card is still blocked." | Try again, order a physical card |
| Wallet unsupported | "Your phone does not support a wallet. Use the card details for online payments." | Show details |
| Refused (account limits) | Reason in plain words and what to do | Contact support |

## UI copy
- Block heading: "Pay today"
- Text: "Get a virtual card now. It works in your phone wallet and online until the new card arrives."
- Buttons: "Get a virtual card" · "Add to phone wallet" · "Not now"
- Done: "Ready to pay with your phone."
- **Needs legal review:** any statement about limits, fees or validity of the virtual card.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a permanent block succeeded, When the confirmation opens, Then "Pay today" is visible without scrolling on a 375×667 screen.
- Given the user taps "Get a virtual card", When issuance succeeds, Then "Add to phone wallet" appears in the same flow.
- Given issuance fails, When the error shows, Then it states the old card remains blocked and offers retry.
- Given the user skips, When they later open home, Then the offer is reachable from the card tile.
- Given a virtual card is active, When the user opens home, Then the tile shows it as ready to pay.

## Analytics
`pay_today_offer_shown{entry}` · `virtual_card_requested` · `virtual_card_issued{ms}` · `virtual_card_issue_failed{reason}` · `virtual_card_added_to_wallet{wallet}` · `pay_today_skipped`.

## Test cases
- Permanent block → offer shown → card issued → added to wallet → home tile shows it.
- Negative: issuance error → message says old card still blocked → retry works.
- Negative: phone without wallet → card details shown, no wallet button.
- Temporary block → offer not shown (old card can be unblocked).
- Accessibility: screen reader announces "Pay today" section and button names; works at 200 % font size.

## Do not break
- s5 relief: "card is blocked" stays first; the offer sits below it.
- Owner vision V2 becomes covered by steps 5a–5b.

## Owner decisions
- Owner decision 1: can the bank issue an instant virtual card after a permanent block? If no, the goal becomes "the user knows how and when they can pay" and the verdict becomes Redesign.
- Fee, limits and validity of the virtual card.

## Dependencies and effort
Card issuing API, wallet provisioning, legal copy. **L**: may need new backend and wallet integration.

# G-02 · P0 · A failed block says the card is NOT blocked and offers a way out

## Problem
If the provider does not confirm the block, the app shows a generic error. The card stays active and the user has no next step (b1.s1). The normal wait (s4) has a spinner with unknown duration.
Findings: CJM-07 (critical, provided), EDGE-01 (critical, provided), CJM-08 (medium, provided), LOAD-03 (high, low confidence: the 30 s wait comes from normalization).

## Goal and metric
- Failed block attempts resolved (blocked on retry or call started) within 10 min · now: not measured · target: ≥ 95 % · how: `card_block_failed` → `card_blocked` or `hotline_call_tapped`.
- Failures that show the "NOT blocked" state · target: 100 %.
- First task: log block duration to set the expected-time text and the timeout.

## Scope
- s4 wait → expected time and a timeout.
- b1.s1 → new failure state with retry and a 24/7 line (branch e1).
- s5 → plain-language confirmation (also closes P2 CJM-09, LOAD-06).
- Out of scope: blocking without the app (P2, EDGE-11).

## TO BE journey (fragment)
| Step | User does | Sees | Response | Undo / way back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | Taps "Block card" | "Blocking card •• 1234… usually takes N seconds" | Block request (idempotent) | — |
| 3a | — | "Your card is NOT blocked yet" · Try again · Call 24/7 block line | Timeout after T s or provider error | Try again |
| 3b | Taps "Try again" | Same progress, "Attempt 2" | Repeats the same request | Call |
| 3c | Taps "Call 24/7 block line" | Phone dialer with the number | — | Back to app |
| 4 | Reads confirmation | "Card •• 1234 is blocked. Nobody can pay with it." | — | — |

## States
| State | What the user sees | What they can do |
|---|---|---|
| Loading | Progress text with expected time | Wait |
| Slow (over N s) | "Still working. Your card is not blocked until you see a confirmation." | Wait, call |
| Error / timeout | "Your card is NOT blocked yet" | Try again, call |
| Offline | "No connection. Your card is NOT blocked yet." | Retry on reconnect, call |
| Success | Plain confirmation | Continue |

## UI copy
- Progress: "Blocking card •• 1234…" / "Usually takes about N seconds."
- Error heading: "Your card is NOT blocked yet"
- Error text: "Try again or call us. The line works 24/7."
- Buttons: "Try again" · "Call 24/7 block line"
- Success: "Card •• 1234 is blocked. Nobody can pay with it."
- No codes: never show BLOCKED_PERM or an error code as the main text.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the provider returns an error, When the app shows the result, Then the heading says the card is NOT blocked.
- Given no response within T s, When the timeout fires, Then the failure state appears with both actions.
- Given the user taps "Try again", When the request repeats, Then no duplicate block or order is created.
- Given two failed attempts, When the second error shows, Then "Call 24/7 block line" is the primary button.
- Given success, When the confirmation shows, Then it names the card's last 4 digits and contains no internal status code.

## Analytics
`card_block_started` · `card_block_succeeded{ms, attempt}` · `card_block_failed{reason, ms, attempt}` · `card_block_retry` · `hotline_call_tapped{after_attempt}`.

## Test cases
- Provider error → "NOT blocked" → retry → success.
- Timeout → failure state at T s, not a spinner forever.
- Network drops during the request → offline state; status re-checked on reconnect.
- Negative: double tap on "Try again" sends one request.
- Accessibility: failure heading announced as an alert by a screen reader.

## Do not break
- s5 relief "money is safe" stays the first thing after success.

## Owner decisions
- 24/7 block line number and whether it works without identification.
- Timeout T and the expected time N, after measuring block duration.

## Dependencies and effort
Provider error codes, idempotency key, telemetry. **M**: client states plus backend timeout and idempotency.

# G-03 · P0 · Blocking starts with one tap from the home screen

## Problem
Owner vision V1: "blocking takes one tap from the home screen". The map needs a tap on the card tile, then card settings with 9 actions, then "Block card", then a choice dialog (s1–s3). s2 is the load peak for every profile (index 36.6 for the main persona, 45.8 for low/low).
Findings: CJM-02 (critical, provided), LOAD-04 (medium, provided).

## Goal and metric
- Taps from home to "card blocked" · now: 4 (map) · target: 2 (entry + confirm) · how: count of `ui_tap` between `home_shown` and `card_blocked`.
- Time from app open to confirmed block · now: 10.6 s KLM model for s1–s3 · target: median ≤ 20 s in real use, baseline to capture · how: `app_open` → `card_blocked`.

## Scope
- s1 → card tile shows "Lost or stolen?".
- s2 → removed from the main path; the 9-action screen stays reachable for other tasks.
- s3 → opens directly, permanent preselected (labels: G-06).
- Out of scope: the content of the dialog options (G-06).

## TO BE journey (fragment)
| Step | User does | Sees | Response | Undo / way back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Opens the app | Home; card tile with "Lost or stolen?" | — | — |
| 2 | Taps "Lost or stolen?" | Block dialog for card •• 1234, permanent preselected | — | Cancel |
| 3 | Taps "Block card" | Progress (G-02) | Block request | — |

## States
| State | What the user sees | What they can do |
|---|---|---|
| Default | "Lost or stolen?" on each card tile | Open the dialog |
| Several cards | Each tile has its own action with last 4 digits | Pick the right card |
| Card already blocked | Tile says "Blocked" with "Order a new card" | Go to reissue (G-07) |

## UI copy
- Tile action: "Lost or stolen?"
- Dialog heading: "Block card •• 1234"
- Primary button: "Block card" · secondary: "Cancel"

## Acceptance criteria
- Given an active card, When home loads, Then "Lost or stolen?" is visible on its tile without scrolling.
- Given the user taps it, When the dialog opens, Then it names the card's last 4 digits and permanent is preselected.
- Given the dialog is open, When the user taps "Block card", Then the block starts with no further screens.
- Given the user taps "Cancel", Then they return to home with nothing changed.
- Given a blocked card, When home loads, Then the tile shows "Blocked" and no "Lost or stolen?".

## Analytics
`lost_card_entry_tapped{source=home_tile|card_screen}` · `block_dialog_opened{preselected}` · `block_dialog_cancelled` · `card_blocked{type, taps, ms_from_open}`.

## Test cases
- Home → "Lost or stolen?" → "Block card" → progress: 2 taps.
- Entry from the card screen still works.
- Two cards: each tile opens the dialog for its own card.
- Negative: "Cancel" leaves the card active and logs `block_dialog_cancelled`.
- Accessibility: the tile action has an accessible name with the card digits; target size ≥ 44×44 pt.

## Do not break
- The confirmation tap stays: the block is irreversible (useful friction, LOAD-05).
- Other card actions remain on the card screen.

## Owner decisions
- Owner decision 4: does V1 "one tap" include the confirmation? Default: one tap opens the dialog, the confirm tap stays.

## Dependencies and effort
Home tile layout, deep link into the dialog. **M**: changes the home screen used by every user.

# G-04 · P1 · Fee and delivery date are known before the order form

## Problem
The reissue fee and "delivery in 5–7 days" appear for the first time on the order summary at confirmation (s8). Owner vision V3 asks for a delivery date before confirming. The s8 dip (emotion −1) is "a week without a card, and a fee nobody mentioned".
Findings: CJM-05 (high, provided), CJM-04 (high, med, provided), LOAD-02 (high, med, provided), EDGE-13 (medium, synthetic).

## Goal and metric
- Orders where fee and delivery date were shown before s6 · now: 0 % · target: 100 % · how: `reissue_terms_shown` before `reissue_form_opened`.
- Drop-off on the summary (s8) · now: not measured · target: −30 % from baseline · how: `reissue_summary_shown` without `reissue_confirmed`.

## Scope
- s5 → "Order a new card" shows fee and "arrives by <date>".
- s8 → repeats the same values; nothing new appears on the summary.
- Out of scope: the fee policy itself and the delivery commitment (owner decisions 2, 3).

## TO BE journey (fragment)
| Step | User does | Sees | Response | Undo / way back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | Reads the block confirmation | "Order a new card · <fee or Free> · arrives by Thu 6 Nov" | — | — |
| 8 | Confirms the order | Summary: same fee, same date, address (G-08) | Order accepted | Back to edit |

## States
| State | What the user sees | What they can do |
|---|---|---|
| Default | Fee and date on the entry and summary | Order |
| Date unavailable | "Arrives in 5–7 working days" with earliest date | Order |
| Fee waived | "Free" | Order |
| Values changed between s5 and s8 | Changed value highlighted with a note | Confirm or go back |

## UI copy
- Entry: "Order a new card" / "<fee> · arrives by <weekday day month>"
- Summary rows: "Fee", "Arrives by", "Delivery address"
- Waived: "Free for lost or stolen cards" — **needs legal review**
- Changed: "The delivery date has changed to <date>."

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a permanent block, When the confirmation shows "Order a new card", Then fee and delivery date are on the same element.
- Given the user reaches the summary, When it renders, Then fee and date equal the values shown at s5 or are highlighted as changed.
- Given no exact date is available, When the entry renders, Then it shows a range with the earliest calendar date.
- Given the fee is zero, Then the entry says "Free", not "0".

## Analytics
`reissue_terms_shown{fee, delivery_date, place=entry|summary}` · `reissue_form_opened` · `reissue_summary_shown` · `reissue_confirmed` · `reissue_terms_changed{field}`.

## Test cases
- Entry and summary show the same fee and date.
- Date changes between entry and summary → highlighted.
- Negative: delivery service unavailable → range shown, no empty field.
- Accessibility: fee and date are read as text, not only as an icon or color.

## Do not break
- s8 summary stays as the final check (useful friction).

## Owner decisions
- Owner decision 2: fee rule for lost or stolen cards.
- Owner decision 3: concrete date vs range; needs a logistics commitment.

## Dependencies and effort
Fee and delivery-estimate API, copy review. **M**: needs a delivery estimate before the form.

# G-05 · P1 · A relative knows on one screen what they may do for the cardholder

## Problem
The frame names a relative acting for an elderly parent, but the map has no path or policy for representatives. Persona p3 (synthetic) asked "Is it even mine to do this?".
Finding: EDGE-05 (high, med, absent). Most of the fix depends on owner decision 5.

## Goal and metric
- Relatives in a test who name the allowed action within 1 min · now: not measured · target: ≥ 4 of 5 · how: usability test (validation task 7).
- Sessions opening "Acting for someone else?" that end in an allowed route (block, call) · target: ≥ 90 % · how: `representative_info_opened` → `card_blocked` or `hotline_call_tapped`.

## Scope
- s2 block dialog → link "Acting for someone else?".
- New info screen with the policy and routes.
- Out of scope: power-of-attorney flows and account access for third parties (adjacent journey).

## TO BE journey (fragment)
| Step | User does | Sees | Response | Undo / way back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Taps "Acting for someone else?" | What a relative may do, what only the cardholder may do, how to call | — | Back |
| 2a | Taps "Call 24/7 block line" | Dialer | — | Back |

## States
| State | What the user sees | What they can do |
|---|---|---|
| Default | Policy in 3 lines with routes | Call, go back |
| Logged in as cardholder (helped by a relative) | Note: "You can block it here yourself" | Return to dialog |

## UI copy
- Link: "Acting for someone else?"
- Heading: "Helping a family member"
- Lines (default option, **needs legal review**): "You can ask us to block their card by phone, 24/7." / "Only the cardholder can order a new card or change the address."
- Button: "Call 24/7 block line"

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the block dialog, When it renders, Then "Acting for someone else?" is visible.
- Given the user opens it, When the screen shows, Then it states what a relative may and may not do in at most 3 lines.
- Given the user taps call, Then the dialer opens with the block line.

## Analytics
`representative_info_opened` · `hotline_call_tapped{source=representative}`.

## Test cases
- Link → info → call.
- Negative: relative tries to change the address in the cardholder's session → the address change follows owner decision 5.
- Accessibility: the info screen works at 200 % font size without horizontal scroll.

## Do not break
- The main path for the cardholder gains no extra step: the link is secondary.

## Owner decisions
- Owner decision 5: may a relative block, order or change the address? Options: phone only; in-app with confirmation from the cardholder; formal power of attorney.

## Dependencies and effort
Policy and legal copy. **S** for the screen; the policy itself is outside design.

# G-06 · P1 · Choosing a block type cannot strand the user without a new card

## Problem
The dialog asks "temporarily or permanently?" without saying what each does (s3, moment of truth). The map's failure note: a temporary block does not allow a new card later; recovery unknown. 2 of 3 synthetic personas could not tell the options apart; the 66-year-old persona chose temporary because "permanent" read as irreversible.
Findings: CJM-06 (high, provided), EDGE-03 (high, med, synthetic). LOAD-05 is a constraint: keep the choice (useful friction).

## Goal and metric
- Temporary blocks from "Lost or stolen" followed by a permanent block or reissue within 24 h · now: not measured · target: < 5 % · how: `card_blocked{type=temporary, entry=lost}` → `card_block_upgraded`.
- Temporary blocks with a route to reissue · now: none · target: 100 %.

## Scope
- s3 dialog → outcome labels, permanent preselected from the "Lost or stolen" entry, irreversibility stated.
- Temporarily blocked card → "Block for good and order a new card" available (branch e3).
- Out of scope: cancelling an order (deferred, EDGE-09).

## TO BE journey (fragment)
| Step | User does | Sees | Response | Undo / way back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Reads the dialog | Two options, each with one line of outcome; permanent preselected | — | Cancel |
| 2' | Picks temporary | "Card paused. You can unpause it or block it for good." | Temporary block | Unpause |
| e3 | Later taps "Block for good and order a new card" | Confirmation, then G-04 entry | Permanent block | — |

## States
| State | What the user sees | What they can do |
|---|---|---|
| Entry from "Lost or stolen" | Permanent preselected | Confirm or switch |
| Entry from card settings | No preselection | Choose |
| Temporarily blocked | Tile "Paused" | Unpause, block for good |

## UI copy
- Option 1: "Block for good and get a new card" / "Nobody can pay with this card again. We send you a new one."
- Option 2: "Pause the card" / "Use this if you may find it. You can unpause it any time. No new card."
- Button: "Block card"
- Paused tile: "Card paused" · "Unpause" · "Block for good"

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the dialog opens from "Lost or stolen", Then permanent is preselected.
- Given either option, Then its line states whether it can be undone and whether a new card follows.
- Given a paused card, When the user opens it, Then "Block for good" leads to the reissue entry.
- Given permanent is chosen, Then no screen says it can be undone.

## Analytics
`block_dialog_opened{entry, preselected}` · `block_type_selected{type, changed_from_default}` · `card_block_upgraded` · `card_unpaused`.

## Test cases
- Lost entry → default permanent → reissue offered.
- Pause → later "Block for good" → reissue entry.
- Negative: pause → user expects a new card → tile shows how to get one.
- Accessibility: options are radio buttons with labels read in full by a screen reader.

## Do not break
- The deliberate confirmation tap on an irreversible action (LOAD-05).

## Owner decisions
- Owner decision 6: upgrade temporary to permanent in the app and allow reissue.

## Dependencies and effort
Block-type upgrade on the backend, copy. **M**: new transition between block states.

# G-07 · P1 · The blocked card and the order stay visible until the new card is active

## Problem
After blocking, the home screen loses the card tile (s10). If the user leaves between blocking and ordering, the route back to reissue is not described. After the order, status depends on one push (s9), and issuer rejection is not described. The map stops at "closes the app".
Findings: CJM-10 (high, absent), CJM-15 (medium, absent), EDGE-04 (high, med, provided).

## Goal and metric
- Users with a blocked card or pending order who see its status on home at the next visit · now: 0 % (tile removed) · target: 100 % · how: `home_card_status_shown{state}`.
- "Where is my card" contacts per 100 orders · now: not measured · target: −30 % from baseline · how: support tags.

## Scope
- s10 home → status tile for the card until the new one is activated.
- s9 → in-app order status and a rejection state.
- Push reminder if the card is blocked and no order is placed (branch e5).
- Out of scope: activation and PIN flow details (adjacent journey).

## TO BE journey (fragment)
| Step | User does | Sees | Response | Undo / way back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 9 | Opens home after blocking, no order | Tile "Card •• 1234 blocked · Order a new card" | — | — |
| 9' | Opens home after ordering | Tile "New card ordered · arrives by <date>" | Push on status change | Track order |
| 9'' | Order rejected by issuer | Tile "We could not order your card" with reason | — | Try again, contact us |

## States
| State | What the user sees | What they can do |
|---|---|---|
| Blocked, no order | Tile with "Order a new card" | Order |
| Ordered | Date and status | Track |
| Shipped | "On its way, arrives by <date>" | Track |
| Delivered | "Activate your new card" | Activate |
| Rejected | Reason and next step | Retry, contact |

## UI copy
- "Card •• 1234 blocked" / "Order a new card"
- "New card ordered" / "Arrives by <date>"
- "We could not order your card" / "<reason in plain words>" / "Try again"
- Reminder push: "Your card is blocked. Order a new one in the app."

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a blocked card without an order, When home loads, Then the tile offers "Order a new card".
- Given an order, When home loads, Then the tile shows status and date without opening push.
- Given the issuer rejects the order, Then the tile shows the rejection with a next step within 1 min of the event.
- Given no order 24 h after blocking, Then one reminder push is sent.

## Analytics
`home_card_status_shown{state}` · `reissue_order_status_changed{from, to}` · `reissue_order_rejected{reason}` · `reissue_reminder_sent` · `reissue_started{entry=home_tile|reminder|confirmation}`.

## Test cases
- Block → leave → reopen → order from the tile.
- Order → status changes → tile updates without push.
- Negative: issuer rejection → state with retry.
- Negative: push disabled → status still visible in the app.
- Accessibility: status text not conveyed by color alone.

## Do not break
- Virtual card tile from G-01 stays next to the order status.

## Owner decisions
- Issuer rejection reasons that may be shown to users.

## Dependencies and effort
Order status API from the issuer, home tile states. **M**.

# G-08 · P1 · An unchanged address is confirmed without typing and shown on the summary

## Problem
The user types a full delivery address on a phone in a moving train (s7): about 40 keystrokes, 25.3 of 45.2 s of the model's KLM time. The summary (s8) does not show the address, so a wrong or outdated one goes unnoticed.
Findings: LOAD-01 (high, med, provided), CJM-13 (medium, med, provided), EDGE-06 (high, med, synthetic).

## Goal and metric
- Orders with the address confirmed without typing · now: 0 % · target: ≥ 80 % · how: `reissue_address_confirmed{source=profile}` / `reissue_confirmed`.
- Time on the address step for an unchanged address · now: 25.3 s (KLM model) · target: median ≤ 5 s · how: `reissue_address_shown` → `reissue_address_confirmed`.
- Cards returned for a wrong address · now: not measured · target: baseline first.

## Scope
- s6–s7 → address from the profile preselected, Edit opens the existing field with suggestions.
- s8 → summary shows the address with Edit.
- Out of scope: card design and name fields (P2, owner decision 7).

## TO BE journey (fragment)
| Step | User does | Sees | Response | Undo / way back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | Opens the order form | "Deliver to: <address> · from your profile" | — | Back |
| 7 | Taps "Use this address" or "Edit" | Edit: field with suggestions | — | Cancel edit |
| 8 | Reads summary | Fee, date, address with Edit | — | Edit |

## States
| State | What the user sees | What they can do |
|---|---|---|
| Profile address exists | Prefilled, marked "from your profile" | Confirm, edit |
| No profile address | Empty field with suggestions | Type |
| Offline while editing | Draft kept, "We will save it when you are back online" | Continue later |
| Undeliverable address | Reason and suggestion | Edit |

## UI copy
- "Deliver to" / "<address>" / "From your profile"
- Buttons: "Use this address" · "Edit"
- Summary row: "Delivery address" · "Edit"

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a profile address, When the form opens, Then it is preselected and marked "from your profile".
- Given the user taps "Use this address", Then no keyboard opens.
- Given the summary, Then the full address is shown with Edit.
- Given the user edits on the summary, Then they return to the summary with the new address.
- Given the connection drops while editing, Then the typed draft is kept.

## Analytics
`reissue_address_shown{source}` · `reissue_address_confirmed{source=profile|edited, ms}` · `reissue_address_edited{place=form|summary}`.

## Test cases
- Profile address → confirm → summary shows it.
- User moved: edit on summary → new address saved for the order.
- Negative: no profile address → typing with suggestions.
- Accessibility: Edit buttons have names with context ("Edit delivery address").

## Do not break
- The summary remains the final check before ordering.

## Owner decisions
- Whether an edited address updates the profile or only this order.

## Dependencies and effort
Profile address API, form state. **M**.
